pattern.crimePattern: credit buyer paying with forged deposit slips kills the wholesaler who noticed
pattern.notes: Fictional mall, bank and businesses on a real street. Casting reviewed in Part C: Somali victim and helpers, none as the culprit.

ob.reportedBy: Fatuma Ali, tea seller, Barwaqo Mall
ob.text: Fatuma Ali, a tea seller, reports that Hodan Farah (34), fabric wholesaler, stall 2-14, Barwaqo Mall, First Avenue, Eastleigh, was found dead in her stall's storage cubicle at 19:05, shortly after the mall closed.

people.name: Hodan Farah
people.bio: Sells printed cotton by the bale to retailers from all over Kenya. Gives credit to buyers she trusts.

image.brief: Somali Kenyan woman, mid 30s, patterned headscarf in deep green, a measuring tape around her neck, bolts of bright printed cotton behind her, shrewd and warm, ID-photo framing

people.name: Josephine Mueni
people.bio: Buys fabric on credit from Hodan and pays by bank deposit slip. Has done for five years.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 50s, a bright purple headscarf tied high, a large woven market bag on her shoulder, reading glasses, composed smile that does not reach her eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Abdirahman Mohamed
people.occupation: Hodan's cousin and co-owner of the stall
people.bio: He and Hodan are in a dispute over her late father's share of the business. The elders are mediating.

image.brief: Somali Kenyan man, mid 40s, trimmed beard, white kanzu and a dark waistcoat, prayer cap, grave and tired, ID-photo framing

people.name: Rajesh Patel
people.bio: Supplies Hodan from his godown in Industrial Area. They argued last month over his new prices.

image.brief: Kenyan Asian man, late 50s, grey hair, short-sleeved checked shirt, a pen and a calculator in his breast pocket, businesslike and impatient, ID-photo framing

people.name: Fatuma Ali
people.bio: Walks the four floors of Barwaqo Mall all day with two flasks of shaah. Found Hodan.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, about 50, a printed cotton dira dress and a matching scarf, two tall flasks held by their handles, warm but shaken, ID-photo framing

people.name: Lameck Onyancha
people.bio: Pushes a mkokoteni in the lanes behind First Avenue. Carries bales to the matatu stages.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 30s, wiry, a sleeveless T-shirt under an open shirt, a rope coiled over one shoulder, sweat on his brow, watchful, ID-photo framing

people.name: Sheikh Ibrahim Hassan
people.bio: Leads prayers at a mosque two streets from the mall.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 60s, a white kanzu and an embroidered white kofia, a neat grey beard, calm and grave, ID-photo framing

locations.name: Barwaqo Mall, First Avenue, Eastleigh
locations.description: Four floors of fabric and clothing stalls. Closing time is 19:00 and the shutters are coming down. Stall 2-14 on the second floor is stacked with bales of printed cotton. A storage cubicle at the back has a plywood door. On the ground floor, a bank branch, its hours painted on the glass.

hotspots.label: Storage cubicle
hotspots.text: Hodan lies between the bales. A steel bale hook is on the floor beside her. A glass of tea stands cold outside the door.

hotspots.label: Invoice book on the counter
hotspots.text: Hodan's carbon invoice book, open at today's page.

hotspots.label: Stapled to the invoice
hotspots.text: A bank deposit slip stapled to the last invoice. Something is written on it in pencil.

hotspots.label: Stall sign
hotspots.text: A painted sign over the stall.

hotspots.label: Letter under the cash box
hotspots.text: A typed letter on a supplier's letterhead, folded twice and weighed down by the cash box.

hotspots.label: Bank glass, ground floor
hotspots.text: The bank branch at the mall entrance. Its opening hours are painted on the glass door.

hotspots.label: Tea seller
hotspots.text: Fatuma Ali sits on an upturned crate with her two flasks, shaking.

hotspots.label: Porters' lane outside
hotspots.text: Behind the mall, the porters' lane. One porter, Lameck Onyancha, is counting coins and watching the police.

image.brief: a wholesale fabric mall corridor in Eastleigh, Nairobi at closing time, stalls stacked with bales of bright printed cotton, shutters half down, fluorescent lights, a plywood storage door at the back of one stall, no people in focus

body.note: Report language only. Struck with a steel bale hook, found on the floor. A glass of tea, cold, outside the door.

image.brief: a cramped storage cubicle stacked with bales of printed fabric, a steel bale hook lying on the cement floor, a small glass of milky tea standing outside the plywood door, no body visible

body.pencil: FAKE? Bank closed. Call in the morning.

image.brief: a bank deposit slip stapled to a carbon invoice, a blue DEPOSITED rubber stamp with the time 17:55, and pencil handwriting in the margin reading "FAKE? Bank closed."

body.text: UMOJA BANK — Eastleigh branch. Mon–Fri 08:30–16:00. Sat 09:00–12:00.
New prices from the 1st, due to the exchange rate. Old prices cannot be honoured. — R. Patel, Patel Textiles, Industrial Area

evidence.title: Amani's note: Josephine at the gate

body.note: Josephine Mueni arrives at the mall gate at 20:30 when called. Purple headscarf. Large woven market bag.

evidence.noPhoto: Amani's own written observation of a person: it stays the note.

items: two blank Umoja Bank deposit slips, already stamped DEPOSITED

image.brief: the contents of a woman's handbag spread on a fabric-stall counter: a purse, a folded market licence, two blank bank deposit slips with blue DEPOSITED stamps, and a plain business card reading MVUA HOLDINGS

facts.text: Hodan Farah was found dead in the storage cubicle of stall 2-14 at 19:05, just after closing.
Hodan was struck with a steel bale hook. It lies on the floor beside her.
Invoice No. 3317: 'J. Mueni — 3 bales printed cotton — 18:20 — paid: bank slip.'
The slip paying invoice 3317: Umoja Bank, KSh 96,000, stamped 'DEPOSITED 17:55'. In Hodan's pencil: 'FAKE? Bank closed. Call in the morning.'
Painted on the bank's glass: Mon–Fri 08:30–16:00. On a Wednesday the bank was shut at 17:55.
The stall is 'Farah & Mohamed Fabrics': Hodan and her cousin Abdirahman Mohamed own it together.
Letter from R. Patel, Patel Textiles: new prices from the 1st, old prices cannot be honoured.
Fatuma brought Hodan tea at 18:25. Hodan was in the cubicle arguing about "the bank" with a woman in a purple headscarf. Fatuma left the glass outside the door.
At 19:05 the tea was still outside the door, cold. Fatuma opened the cubicle and found Hodan.
Fatuma went straight up to the third floor after 18:25; two stallholders there bought tea from her at 18:35.
Lameck: at 18:40 the bales were outside the shut cubicle. A woman in a purple headscarf came out alone: 'Mama Hodan is resting. Don't disturb her.' She paid him KSh 300.
Lameck: the same woman hired him at 18:30 in the lane to carry three bales to the Machakos matatus. He came up at 18:40.
Josephine Mueni is wearing a purple headscarf.
Josephine's handbag holds two blank Umoja Bank deposit slips that are already stamped 'DEPOSITED'.
A business card in her handbag: 'Mvua Holdings — Fast Loans · Title Searches · Document Services — Till 880 214'.
Josephine: "I left Eastleigh at four on the Machakos matatu. By six I was already home."
Josephine: "I have bought from Hodan for five years. Ask anyone in this mall."
Josephine admits she came back to stall 2-14 at 18:20 for three more bales. She says Hodan was alive and shouting when she left at about half past six.
Abdirahman: "I was at the mosque from before Maghrib."
Abdirahman: the dispute over her father's share is with the elders. "It is not a matter for the police."
Abdirahman: Josephine always paid by bank slip. Hodan trusted her and never checked.
Sheikh Ibrahim: Abdirahman came early for Maghrib, about 18:20, and stayed talking with him until about 19:00.
Rajesh: "I haven't been to Eastleigh in a week. I was at my godown all evening."
Rajesh: the price dispute was about the shilling falling. "Nothing personal. Everybody got the same letter."
Patel Textiles gate log, Industrial Area: 'R. Patel — in 17:00 — out 19:30.'

interrogations.intro: Josephine arrives at the gate at half past eight, called back from Machakos road. "Hodan? No. No. Five years I have bought from her."

topics.reply: That is a deposit slip. I deposit, the bank stamps, I pay. Ask the bank.
Maybe they had a late counter. I don't work in a bank.
Many women wear purple. Go to Gikomba and count them.

interrogations.intro: Abdirahman has come straight from the mosque, still barefoot in his sandals. "My cousin. We fought over money. That is family. That is not this."

topics.reply: Our dispute is with the wazee, the elders. Her father's share. We would have settled it in a month.
Mama Josephine from Machakos? She always paid by slip. Hodan trusted her. Hodan never even went to the bank to check.
Ask the Sheikh. I came early for Maghrib and sat with him.

interrogations.intro: Rajesh Patel takes Amani's call in his godown, a forklift beeping behind him. "Who is this? I'm busy."

topics.reply: Everybody got that letter. The shilling falls, I pay more in dollars, the price goes up. Nothing personal.
She was the best buyer on First Avenue. She argued, she paid. I am very sorry.

interrogations.intro: Fatuma holds a flask in each hand as if they might steady her. "I bring her shaah every evening. Every evening."

topics.reply: At twenty-five past six she was arguing about the bank with a woman. A woman in purple. I left the glass outside. I didn't want to disturb.

interrogations.intro: Lameck wipes his palms on his shirt. "I carried bales for a woman. That is my work. I did nothing."

topics.reply: That is the woman. The purple. She told me Mama Hodan was resting. She paid me three hundred and I took her bales to the Machakos matatus.

contradictions.reaction: I came back for the bales, yes. Three bales, that is all. She was alive when I left. She was shouting at me, but she was alive.

prosecutor.pass: A slip from a shut bank, a woman in purple at 18:25 and again at 18:40, and a lie about the matatu. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. A family dispute with the elders isn't a woman in purple in the cubicle. Read the tea seller and the porter together.
No. Who was arguing with her about the bank, and who came out of that cubicle alone?

proof.concludes: Josephine said she was home in Machakos by six, but Hodan wrote her invoice 3317 at 18:20. Pressed, she admits being at the stall at 18:20.
The slip she paid with claims a deposit at 17:55 at a bank that shuts at 16:00. It is fake, and Hodan had noticed: that is why she died.

At 18:25 Hodan was arguing about "the bank" with a woman in a purple headscarf. At 18:40 a woman in a purple headscarf came out of the shut cubicle alone and kept people away. Josephine wears a purple headscarf, and she had the reason. Josephine Mueni killed Hodan.

eliminations.why: Sheikh Ibrahim sat with Abdirahman at the mosque from about 18:20 to 19:00.
Rajesh was in his Industrial Area godown from 17:00 to 19:30.
Fatuma left the tea at 18:25 and was selling on the third floor at 18:35; the woman she heard arguing was someone else.
Lameck was in the lane until 18:40 and arrived to find the cubicle already shut.

reconstruction.text: For two months Josephine has paid Hodan with deposit slips that were never deposited. This week Hodan starts to look closely.
18:20. Josephine comes back for three more bales with another slip, stamped 17:55. Hodan writes invoice 3317, then looks at the stamp. The bank shuts at four.
18:25. In the cubicle, Hodan says she will go to the bank in the morning, and then the police. Fatuma leaves a glass of tea outside the door.
Josephine picks up the bale hook. Then she drags her bales out of the cubicle and shuts the door. At 18:30 she hires a porter in the lane.
18:40. "Mama Hodan is resting. Don't disturb her." She pays the porter KSh 300 and rides to Machakos with the bales.

tier1.line: Hodan wrote on the slip before she died. Then walk down to the ground floor and read the glass.

tier2.line: The tea seller heard a woman at 18:25. The porter saw a woman at 18:40. Describe them both. Then look at who came to the gate.

glossary.def: Mother; also a respectful way to address or name a woman.
Long white robe worn by men.

ui.beatNotes: Signs and notices as evidence: for the first time something painted on a wall (the bank's hours on the glass) is a collectible fact. Teaches the player to read the environment, not just people and papers.
